exposure: Pre-eclampsia diagnosis (severe, mild, or normal pregnancy)
outcome: Expression of micro-144 (miR-144) in peripheral blood
Expression of titin antibody (titin-Ab) in peripheral blood
Expression of p-p38 protein in placenta tissues
Expression of phosphorylated c-Jun N-terminal kinase (p-JNK) protein in placenta tissues
Expression of phosphorylated extracellular regulated protein kinases (p-ERK) protein in placenta tissues
cohort: The study included 58 pre-eclampsia patients (31 severe, 27 mild) and 30 normal pregnant women as controls.
finding: Pre-eclampsia patients showed significantly decreased miR-144 and increased titin-Ab, along with altered MAPK pathway protein (p-p38, p-JNK, p-ERK) expression in placenta, with these changes correlating with disease severity and suggesting an important role in pre-eclampsia development.
cross-section timing: Samples (peripheral blood and placenta tissues) were collected after cesarean section for placental tissues, and likely at the time of diagnosis or during pregnancy for blood samples.
